title: Current Evidence Base
subtitle: What research supports and what remains uncertain
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating current evidence base across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
learningObjectives: Explain current evidence base in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in current evidence base.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to current evidence base.

sections.explainSimply: EMDR is an evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapy for PTSD and is recommended in major clinical guidance.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Comparative evidence does not show EMDR to be consistently superior to other bona fide psychological treatments for PTSD; treatment preference, fit, access and dropout still matter.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: The evidence supports EMDR as a treatment approach for PTSD, not a uniquely proven neural mechanism. Mechanistic accounts—including working-memory taxation, orienting responses and memory updating—remain active areas of research.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of current evidence base as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need current evidence base to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Guideline support does not mean universal benefit or zero risk.
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use current evidence base to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses current evidence base to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Guideline support establishes treatment legitimacy, not universal benefit, superiority over every alternative, or a uniquely established neural mechanism. Evidence classification: established PTSD treatment efficacy; mechanism uncertainty remains.
